newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Securities Commission seeks price-fix probe.
newsitem.headline: Polish Securities Commission seeks price-fix probe.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices on the Warsaw bourse, a deputy KPW head told private Radio Zet on Tuesday.
"We've sent notice of a suspicion that the crime...of manipulation has been committed, which is punishable under the law on public trading of securities," Zofia Bielecka was quoted as saying.
Bourse head Wieslaw Rozlucki told the radio station the case might be the most significant since Warsaw resumed bourse trade in 1991, following the 1989 fall of communism.
"It looks like a serious matter -- there haven't yet been cases (involving) so many individuals," Rozlucki said.
He said that each year the bourse informs the KPW of 30 to 40 cases in which prices rise sharply for no apparent reason.
No one at the Securities Commission (KPW) was immediately available for comment.
